details.description: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp, released August 21, 2026, was DeepSeek's first experimental multimodal model in the V4 family, described on its own Hugging Face model card as built on the DeepSeek-V4-Flash architecture (305 billion parameters) with an added vision encoder and aligner so it can process images and text together. DeepSeek's model card states it achieves comparable performance to DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on text-only agent tasks while substantially improving multimodal agent capabilities, and its own benchmark table shows those multimodal agent scores approaching, and on some benchmarks matching or exceeding, Claude Opus-4.8's scores on the same tests. DeepSeek retired the model on September 10, 2026, and requests to the id deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are now routed to the newer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, billed at Flash pricing.
advantages: Scores 83.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, an agentic terminal-use benchmark, per DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card.
Resolves 75.9% of tasks on Toolathlon-Verified, a tool-use agent benchmark.
Natively processes images alongside text via an added vision encoder and aligner, rather than a text-only base.

DeepSeek's Hugging Face model card shows its multimodal agent scores approaching or exceeding Claude Opus-4.8's on the same benchmarks, e.g. 83.9 vs. 85.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 59.3 vs. 58.0 on DeepSWE, while matching DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on text-only agent tasks.
disadvantages: Explicitly labeled experimental by DeepSeek, as an early multimodal expansion of DeepSeek-V4-Flash still undergoing continued training.
DeepSeek retired this model on September 10, 2026, routing deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp requests to the newer DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash.
Scores lower than DeepSeek's later DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on comparable agent benchmarks, e.g. 83.9 vs. 90.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 59.3 vs. 74.2 on DeepSWE.
use_cases: Visual-understanding agent tasks that combine images with tool use.
Agentic terminal and software-engineering tasks (Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSWE) that also require reading visual content.
General text-only agentic tasks at capability comparable to DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731.

notes: Catalog's modality (image_input + text_input + text_output) matches this model's own vision-capable design (not just inherited routing, unlike the plain deepseek-v4-flash id). Benchmark comparisons to DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in disadvantages use that model's own Hugging Face card figures, opened separately, for the same benchmark names. Left out several other agent benchmarks on the card (ApexBench, Agents' Last Exam, ZeroBench) for brevity since Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSWE, Toolathlon-Verified and Chartography already cover the same kind of evidence; all are 0-100 pass-rate style scores. A precise release-day parameter count beyond the card's overall '305B' figure, and an exact context-window token number, were not stated on the pages read, so neither is claimed beyond the catalog's own facts. Corrected on verification: the Opus-4.8 comparison and the 'matches DeepSeek-V4-Flash on text capabilities' claim are on the model's own Hugging Face card (its 'Comparison with frontier models' table), not on the change log/release notes as the file previously said; the change log's Aug 21 entry only announces the model, with no Opus-4.8 or text-capability-parity language. The card's own comparison table gives specific per-benchmark scores for the Opus-4.8 comparison (e.g. 83.9 vs. 85.0 on Terminal-Bench 2.1; the model actually exceeds Opus-4.8 on DeepSWE, 59.3 vs. 58.0), so the description and advantages now cite those numbers instead of the vaguer 'approached the level of' language. Also removed 'reasoning' and 'world knowledge' from the text-capability-parity claim: the card only states comparable performance on text-only agent tasks, and compares this model against DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 specifically (not the generic DeepSeek-V4-Flash preview) for that parity claim. Checked whether the 'DeepSWE' vs. 'DeepSWE v1.1' naming difference in the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash disadvantages comparison was a version mismatch: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's own comparison table lists 'DeepSWE v1.1' scores including a 'DS-V4-Flash' column of 54.4, which is exactly DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731's own (unversioned) DeepSWE score on its own card -- so DeepSeek treats the unversioned and v1.1-labeled scores as the same benchmark run, and the 59.3 vs. 74.2 comparison in disadvantages was kept unchanged.
